binders: First conjunct: an arbitrary type Ω with a measurable space, a probability measure μ, a function X:Ω→Real, and a real number B.
Second conjunct: an independently arbitrary type Ω with a measurable space, a probability measure μ, a function X:Ω→Real, and, in the conclusion, every real p.
hypotheses: First conjunct: X is measurable, B>0, and |X(ω)|≤B for μ-almost every ω.
Second conjunct: X is measurable, LocalDef001 μ X<∞, and p≥1.
conclusions: Every measurable, almost-everywhere B-bounded real random variable with B>0 has LocalDef001 μ X<∞.
If LocalDef001 μ X<∞, then for every real p≥1 the function ω↦|X(ω)|^p, using real exponentiation, is μ-integrable.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X is inf{t∈ENNReal : LocalDef002 μ X t}.
LocalDef002 μ X t means that X is measurable, t≠0, t≠∞, ω↦exp(X(ω)^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2.
The relation LocalDef001 μ X<∞ means this ENNReal-valued infimum is finite.
Integrable means almost-everywhere strong measurability together with finite integral norm.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For probability measures, the conjunction states: first, every measurable real-valued function that is almost surely bounded in absolute value by some positive B has a finite infimum of positive finite scales t for which exp(X²/t²) is integrable with integral at most 2; second, whenever that infimum is finite, every real absolute moment |X|^p with p≥1 is integrable.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The two conjuncts quantify independently over Ω, its measurable structure, μ, and X.
The measure must be a probability measure and X must be measurable in both conjuncts.
The boundedness hypothesis is only μ-almost everywhere and requires a strictly positive B.
Admissible scales explicitly exclude both 0 and ∞ before applying ENNReal.toReal.
The infimum need not itself be an admissible scale or be attained.
The second conclusion covers real exponents p≥1, with exponentiation interpreted as Real.rpow, not merely integer powers.
The statement proves qualitative integrability only; it supplies no explicit bound on the p-th moment.
Finiteness of the infimum is an encoded scale condition rather than an explicit existential witness in the target.
ambiguities: The dossier does not supply an intended conventional name for LocalDef001; its explicit infimum definition is nevertheless unambiguous.
